NEW DELHI: The captain of Air India’s August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet, was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival, whose result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.TOI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as serious and said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.“Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,” it said.Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules stipulate that “in case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety-sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisation” for de-addiction.Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. “As standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing. Samples have been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,” the ministry statement added.Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.
Article Summary: The captain of air india’s august 4 phuket-delhi flight was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival. The result was “not negative” and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said sunday. Toi had exclusively reported on sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.

Article Title: Captain of turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight may have failed dope test
Article Text:
The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet.

NEW DELHI: The captain operating Air India’s turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight on Tuesday (Aug 4) reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival, according to multiple sources. The airline did not either confirm or deny it, saying while the tests were conducted, the results have not been shared with it.“We are aware that a post-flight screening test was conducted on the pilots in accordance with applicable protocols. However, the results of the test have not been shared with Air India, and we are therefore not in a position to comment on any findings,” an AI spokesperson said.“Air India undertakes regular drug testing of crew members in compliance with civil aviation regulations, independent of any specific flight or operational incident. We will continue to cooperate with the relevant authorities as required,” the airline added.The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. Sources say the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.Pending probe, flight crew is taken off flying duty as per protocol. So the pilots of this flight are also not flying currently. DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.But after resuming flying if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances again, their licence will be suspended for three years. And if after resuming flying the same person again tests positive for the third time, the flying licence is cancelled.International Civil Aviation Organisation says that “holders of licences shall not exercise the privileges of their licences and related ratings while under the influence of any psychoactive substance, which might render them unable to safely and properly exercise these privileges”.While the probe in Tuesday’s event would have focused on pilot handling the situation anyway, the captain reportedly testing positive adds another dimension to the same.
Article Summary: The captain operating air india’s turbulence-hit phuket-delhi flight reportedly tested positive in a psychoactive substances (dope) test conducted on arrival. The airbus a320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised.

Article Title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: On July 1, an attack by pirates on an India-bound bulk carrier, Golden Arsenal, in the Gulf of Aden was foiled after the captain moved all crew members, including an Indian seafarer, into the vessel’s “citadel” and sought assistance from the Indian Navy A citadel is a fortified safe room with essential supplies such as food and water, as well as communication equipment, where crew members can take refuge during a pirate attack. The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel.Sharing this incident at the National Port Security Conference this week, Captain Vikram Singh Manhas, deputy nautical adviser at DGMA (maritime regulator), urged all crew members and masters to remain vigilant and follow preventive measures prescribed under best management practices (BMP), amid a rise in piracy incidents.Four vessels are held hostage by Somali pirates at present, three of which have Indian crew members aboard.One of the vessels has one Indian seafarer, while the other two have five and 11 Indian crew, respectively.Highlighting the significance of prevention in such cases, Manhas said that once a vessel is held by pirates, everything is dependent upon the negotiations with the pirates and that the government is working to ensure the safe release of Indian seafarers.In the direction of ensuring their safety, the government is set to launch a dashboard on August 15 to track every Indian seafarer on any ship. Additionally, shipping and ports minister Sarbananda Sonowal Saturday launched e-Samudra, a digital platform integrating services for seafarers, shipping companies, ports and other maritime stakeholders, and said, “Every Indian seafarer must be safe, respected and supported as India strengthens its position as a global maritime power. ”

The pirates failed to breach the citadel and eventually fled the vessel. Four vessels are held hostage by somali pirates at present, three of which have indian crew members aboard.

NEW DELHI: The pilots of Air India’s Aug 4 turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight were subjected to psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival at the destination. The pilot-in-command or captain’s screening test report was not negative and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said on Sunday. During the occurrence, injuries were reported to a few passengers and cabin crew members on board.The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members comprising two pilots and six cabin crew. ”“As standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing. Samples have accordingly been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,” it added.Pending investigation, both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA. “The aviation ministry and DGCA remain firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of aviation safety and ensuring that all such occurrences are thoroughly investigated and appropriate action is taken in accordance with the prescribed regulations and procedures,” the statement added.The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. People in the know say authorities are probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Article Title: ‘Not taking up the position’: VVS Laxman reveals why he turned down India head coach job after Dravid
Article Text:
BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, left, with BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) head VVS Laxman. (PTI Photo)

Laxman defends CoE amid injury concerns

BENGALURU: VVS Laxman has revealed that he turned down the opportunity to succeed Rahul Dravid as India head coach in 2024, choosing instead to continue his work at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and citing family considerations as one of the reasons behind his decision.The BCCI had approached Laxman after Dravid's successful stint ended with India's T20 World Cup triumph in 2024. However, the former India batter opted to extend his tenure at the then National Cricket Academy, which was subsequently rebranded as the CoE, for another two years until 2026.“Because (former BCCI secretary) Jay (Shah) and the BCCI gave me the freedom to execute my vision, and Devajit (Saikia, current BCCI secretary) continues to give me, I've extended (stint at CoE) for two years, and I committed to the BCCI that I'm not taking up the head coach position. You all know that I was approached back in 2024,” Laxman said at a presser at the CoE on Sunday.Laxman, who succeeded Dravid as the head of the NCA in 2021, said he wanted to establish the CoE's structure, processes and protocols before moving on.“I'll make sure that I establish the CoE, its structure, the processes and the protocols... before I move on, after the two years' stay,” he said.His comments come amid speculation that he could be considered for another prominent BCCI role, with his name being linked to the chief selector's position once Ajit Agarkar 's tenure ends in September. Laxman, however, did not indicate any decision on his future beyond his current CoE stint. Laxman also strongly defended the CoE's role amid concerns over the number of India players currently recovering from injuries , insisting that the facility should not be viewed merely as a rehabilitation centre.Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Hardik Pandya, Washington Sundar and B Sai Sudharsan are among the players who have been recuperating at the facility.“CoE is not just a rehab centre, but there are bigger roles to play for it in helping cricketers achieve excellence,” Laxman said, stressing that injuries cannot always follow predetermined recovery timelines because “it is the human body” and “not a machine”.He said there was “seamless” communication between the CoE, selectors and team management, with players released only after meeting prescribed fitness benchmarks.Laxman also highlighted the development of young cricketers and his involvement in women's cricket as major achievements of his tenure.“Trophies are a by-product of what systems and processes you set,” he said, adding that the CoE's work was aimed at strengthening Indian cricket and helping players become the best they can be.
Article Summary: Vvs laxman reveals he turned down the opportunity to succeed rahul dravid as india head coach in 2024. The former india batter opted to continue his work at the bcci centre of excellence (coe) for another two years until 2026. He said he wanted to establish the coe's structure and processes before moving on.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I play tennis for a living even though I hate it” - How Andre Agassi turned a tyrannical childhood into tennis greatness and personal redemption
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “I play tennis for a living even though I hate it” - How Andre Agassi turned a tyrannical childhood into tennis greatness and personal redemption

Andre Agassi became one of tennis’ biggest stars despite saying he hated the sport he played for most of his life. The eight-time Grand Slam champion and 1996 Olympic gold medallist was pushed into tennis by his father, Mike Agassi, when he was very young. His childhood training included a powerful ball machine he called “The Dragon”, which sent balls at about 110 mph. Agassi later wrote in his autobiographyabout the fear, pressure and anger he carried from those years. Yet he went on to become world No. 1, complete a career Grand Slam and build a new purpose through education.For Andre Agassi, tennis was never simply a childhood game. His father, Mike Agassi, wanted one of his children to become a great tennis player and pushed Andre harder than most young players could imagine.Mike had been an Olympic boxer for Iran and brought the same strong approach to training. He built a tennis court at the family home in Las Vegas and made Andre spend long hours hitting balls. The young player was expected to keep going even when he was tired or wanted to stop.The most memorable part of that training was “The Dragon”, a modified ball machine that Mike made more powerful. It could send tennis balls towards Andre at about 110 mph., quoting Agassi’s account in, described how frightening the machine was for the seven-year-old.Agassi later explained his father’s thinking in“My father says that if I hit 2,500 balls a day, I’ll hit 17,500 balls a week, and at the end of one year I’ll have hit nearly one million balls. He says numbers don’t lie. A child who hits one million balls a year will be invincible.”For Mike, the numbers meant progress. For Andre, the endless practice became a source of fear and frustration. He was becoming better at tennis, but he was not developing a love for it.That conflict stayed with him for years. In, Agassi put his feelings into one of the most famous lines from the book:“I play tennis for a living even though I hate tennis, hate it with a dark and secret passion and always have.”The words were striking because they came from a player who would eventually become one of the most successful men in the history of the sport.By the time Andre Agassi reached his teenage years, tennis had already shaped almost every part of his life. At 13, he was sent to Nick Bollettieri’s tennis academy in Florida, where he trained alongside other young players hoping to reach the professional tour. The ATP Tour confirms that Agassi was sent to the academy at that age and turned professional at 16 in 1986.His appearance soon made him stand out. Long hair, bright clothes and a rebellious image made Agassi look like someone who wanted to challenge the traditional image of tennis.But there was a reason that rebellion mattered so much to him.For years, other people had decided what his life should look like. His father decided how much he should train. Tennis decided where he would travel. Coaches decided how he should play. The teenager’s loud style gave him a way to show that there was still a part of his life he could control.The pressure did not disappear after he became a professional. In fact, Agassi later said he had taken his father’s voice and expectations into his own mind.“I’ve internalized my father-his impatience, his perfectionism, his rage. I no longer need my father to torture me. From this day on, I can do it all by myself.”That pressure existed alongside major success. Agassi won his first Grand Slam at Wimbledon in 1992, followed by the US Open in 1994 and the Australian Open in 1995. He also won Olympic singles gold in Atlanta in 1996. By the end of his career, he had collected eight Grand Slam singles titles. Olympedia lists his eight major titles and Olympic gold medal.Still, winning did not automatically make him happy.Agassi’s career later reached a point where the champion everyone knew seemed to be disappearing. In November 1997, his ranking dropped to No. 141. Just two years earlier, he had been world No. 1.The fall was not only about rankings. Agassi had lost his direction and needed to decide whether he still wanted to keep playing.Instead of walking away, he started again at a much lower level. He played Challenger events, where the crowds were smaller and the conditions were far removed from the big stages where he had once been a star.The ATP Tour describes that period as the beginning of his comeback. After reaching No. 141, Agassi finished 1997 by playing Challenger events and then climbed back to No. 6 in 1998.The biggest moment of that comeback came at the 1999 French Open.Agassi won at Roland Garros and completed the career Grand Slam, meaning he had now won all four major singles tournaments. His list already included Wimbledon, the US Open and the Australian Open. The French Open was the missing piece.Winning it changed how his career was viewed. He was no longer simply the talented player with the flashy clothes and huge personality. He had shown that he could fall a long way and still find a way back.That comeback also gave Agassi a different relationship with tennis. He was no longer simply following the path his father had created for him. He had gone through the worst part of his career and chosen to continue.Away from the court, Agassi eventually found another part of his life that mattered to him deeply: education.He established the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education and later launched the Andre Agassi College Preparatory Academy in Las Vegas. The ATP Tour says the school opened in 2001 as a public K-12 charter school serving at-risk young people in his hometown.Agassi’s work with children gave his success a purpose beyond tennis. Instead of using his name only to celebrate what he had achieved, he used it to help young people get opportunities he felt he had missed.His personal life also changed. He married Steffi Graf in 2001. Graf is one of the greatest women’s tennis players ever, with 22 Grand Slam singles titles. Together, Agassi and Graf have continued to support education and charitable work.That change in outlook is reflected in another line from Agassi’s“It’s no accident, I think, that tennis uses the language of life. Advantage, service, fault, break, love, the basic elements of tennis are those of everyday existence, because every match is a life in miniature.”There is a clear link between that thought and Agassi’s own journey. His life had its advantages and faults, its wins and losses, and one major comeback after another.The boy who once wanted to escape tennis eventually became one of its greatest champions. But his story is not simply about learning to love the sport.It is about taking control of a life that had been planned for him.Andre Agassi did not choose tennis as a child. His father chose it for him. Yet after years of pressure, success, failure and a dramatic comeback, Agassi found ways to decide what tennis would mean to him.He finished his career with eight Grand Slam titles, an Olympic gold medal and a career Grand Slam. But his work in education became another important part of what he left behind.His story is inspiring because the difficult beginning did not have to decide the ending. Andre Agassi turned the sport that once represented pressure into a platform for achievement and helping others. That shift, more than any single trophy, explains why his story still carries meaning.
Article Summary: Andre agassi became one of tennis’ biggest stars despite saying he hated the sport he played for most of his life. The eight-time grand slam champion was pushed into tennis by his father, mike agassi, when he was very young. Agassi later wrote in his autobiographyabout the fear, pressure and anger he carried from those years.

NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already made a remarkable impression on the cricketing world at 15, and Australia pace great Brett Lee believes the teenager has everything required to achieve “bigger and better things” — provided he is protected from the pressure accompanying his rapid rise.Sooryavanshi became one of the biggest stories of IPL 2026 after an extraordinary campaign for Rajasthan Royals . The left-hander scored 776 runs in 16 matches to claim the Orange Cap, repeatedly displaying a fearless approach against some of the world's best bowlers.His performances earned him a fast-track call-up to India's T20I side. After a difficult start to international cricket during the England series, Sooryavanshi responded impressively on India's Zimbabwe tour, finishing as Player of the Series.For Lee, however, the teenager's age should not overshadow what he is already doing on the field.Sooryavanshi's age has become a constant talking point outside India, but Lee believes the focus should be on his ability rather than the number attached to his name.“He is incredible. Everyone offshore, away from India, asks the question if he's 15. He is 15 is probably the biggest talking point around the world. I don't care how old he is.If he's 15, fantastic, but if he's 17 or 18, who cares. This kid can play cricket. He has been such a great find for India, and he's going to go on to achieve bigger and better things,” Lee said on the BeerBiceps YouTube channel.The former Australia fast bowler was particularly impressed by Sooryavanshi's ability to take on express pace during the IPL, including against Australian quicks.“He has already lit up the IPL in such a short space of time. That 97 he got (vs SRH), he was up against Aussie bowlers. They were bowling gas, and he was hooking them off his nose. He is playing proper cricketing shots and has power that he finds from somewhere,” Lee said.While Lee sees little reason to worry about Sooryavanshi's batting or current form, he believes the mental side of the game will be the biggest test as expectations continue to grow.“It won't be his form or batting; it'll only be his mind. He still has to be a kid. Let him be a kid and don't put too much pressure,” Lee said.The warning comes after Sooryavanshi's rapid transition from teenage prospect to IPL star and then an India international. The attention surrounding him is only likely to increase as he continues to perform at the highest level.Lee also offered an insight into how he would have approached the challenge of bowling to the teenager, particularly given Sooryavanshi's confidence against short-pitched deliveries.“If someone was a good hooker or puller of the ball, I used to love that because then it becomes a contest. So of course I would go into the boardroom, go upstairs and have a look. I'll put one on his badge and see what he does with it. He might hook me for six, but it won't discourage me from giving him another one,” Lee said.For a player who has already shown he is not intimidated by reputation or pace, such contests could become a defining feature of Sooryavanshi's early career.But Lee's message is clear: the teenager's biggest battle may not be against fast bowlers at all. It may be learning to handle everything that comes with being cricket's latest teenage sensation.
Article Summary: Brett lee believes vaibhav sooryavanshi has everything required to achieve ‘bigger and better things’ the former australia fast bowler believes the mental side of the game will be the biggest test as expectations continue to grow. Lee also offered an insight into how he would have approached the challenge of bowling to the teenager.

‘We don't use the term blame’

NEW DELHI: With India's growing injury list putting the spotlight on the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE), its head VVS Laxman has pushed back against the scrutiny surrounding the Bengaluru-based facility, insisting that injuries are an unavoidable part of a cricketer's career and that the focus should be on monitoring players rather than finding scapegoats.The CoE has come under increasing scrutiny in recent weeks amid concerns over rehabilitation timelines, fitness assessments and communication between its sports science team and the national selection committee. Several key players are currently dealing with injuries, with Jasprit Bumrah, Sai Sudharsan, Harshit Rana, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Washington Sundar among those facing fitness concerns.Laxman, however, defended the institution's broader role, stressing that it should not be reduced to a rehabilitation centre."CoE is not merely a rehab centre. There are bigger roles to play for it in helping cricketers achieve excellence," Laxman said at a press conference in Bengaluru on Sunday.His comments come at a time when the CoE's injury-management programme is under renewed examination, particularly with India set to begin a crucial Test series against Sri Lanka on August 15.Laxman also refused to attribute India's injury problems to any individual or department, arguing that injuries are an inherent part of professional sport."Injuries are part and parcel of any player's career. That's why monitoring system is very critical. And we don't use the term blame then we will be trying to find scapegoats," he said.The CoE chief pointed towards the facility's monitoring systems and the measures being used to assess players continuously, rather than relying solely on conventional fitness tests."Yo Yo test cannot be done when a player is part of the series, so we have introduced Bronco test by Adrian, so that the fitness can be monitored continously," Laxman said.He cited Bumrah and Sudharsan as examples of players whose fitness was assessed through multiple parameters before decisions were made on their availability."Jasprit Bumrah and B Sai Sudharsan were picked as subject to fitness. We move them from one parameter to other before giving the clearance to play. The communication between CoE and team management is quite seamless," he added.The comments are significant given the uncertainty that has surrounded the availability of both Bumrah and Sudharsan for the Sri Lanka Tests.Both players were initially included in India's squad subject to fitness, but the CoE's medical and sports science experts ultimately opted for caution after assessing their respective conditions.Bumrah's absence is particularly significant, with the fast bowler's knee continuing to cause problems after an impact injury. Fluid retention has required additional recovery time, forcing India to prepare for the series without one of their most important Test match-winners.Sudharsan, meanwhile, had been spending considerable time batting in the nets as part of his recovery but continued to experience pain in his left big toe.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia met Laxman at the CoE in Bengaluru on Sunday to take stock of the rehabilitation and injury-management programme.For the BCCI, the concern is not merely the number of players unavailable but also whether the timelines communicated by the CoE have consistently matched the expectations of the selectors.Laxman, however, maintained that the process is centred on continuous assessment and communication rather than assigning blame when a player suffers a setback.With India's injury list growing and a demanding Test season ahead, the CoE is likely to remain under the microscope. Laxman's message was clear: the facility's role is not simply to get injured players back on the field, but to manage their overall journey towards sustained excellence.
Article Summary: Vvs laxman insists that injuries are an unavoidable part of a cricketer's career. Coe has come under increasing scrutiny amid concerns over rehabilitation timelines, fitness assessments and communication between its sports science team and the national selection committee.

Article Title: “Aaron has created this fake universe of....": Aaron Rodgers faces explosive backlash as Nick Wright declares Steelers star 'non-credible'

Aaron Rodgers' latest comments on Dr. Anthony Fauci have once again pushed the veteran quarterback into the middle of a heated public debate. While Rodgers defended his long-held views during a recent appearance on, his remarks prompted a fierce response from FS1 analyst Nick Wright, who questioned both the quarterback's credibility and his continued focus on the issue years after the pandemic.Rodgers revisited one of the most controversial chapters of his career while speaking on. During the conversation, he criticized former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases director Dr. Anthony Fauci, calling him an “absolute coward” for repeatedly invoking the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing led by Sen. Rand Paul.The Steelers quarterback also expanded his criticism to ESPN, despite appearing on a program that airs on the network. Although Pat McAfee and the show's co-hosts attempted to move the discussion elsewhere, Rodgers remained committed to expressing his views.The comments quickly reignited debate around Rodgers' role during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly the controversy surrounding his vaccination status in 2021. At the time, Rodgers said he had been "immunized" but later acknowledged that he had misled people about his vaccination status after testing positive for COVID-19.That history became the focus of Nick Wright's response.Speaking on his podcast, Wright argued that Rodgers has created a false version of events surrounding the criticism he received.“Aaron has created this fake universe of martyrdom where he took a stand no one else was willing to take,” Wright said. “He paid (a) heavy price for it. That’s not what [expletive] happened. Aaron got criticized because he lied without directly lying, knew he was doing it, and people didn’t like that.“Instead of having the courage of his convictions, six years ago, he instead passed the buck, did a play on the words, ‘Yeah, I’ve been immunized,’ and then kept that ruse running until he got caught. That’s what he was criticized for.”Wright did not stop there. He argued that Rodgers has continued fueling the controversy by repeatedly returning to the subject instead of moving on.“To go on top of the fact that he didn’t seem to be a very good leader; a lot of pointing fingers instead of pointing thumbs there was just so much obvious [expletive] that he just became, for a lot of us, a non-credible person and instead of taking any accountability for any of that he’s like, ‘Nope, I just bravely wouldn’t get that toxic shot and now I’ve been proven right and you all owe me an apology.’ It’s just such nonsense. ”“He got more and more criticized because he wouldn’t stop talking about this years later,” Wright said. “And then kept upping the ante on his kooky conspiratorial stuff when he tried to bring Jimmy Kimmel into the Epstein list and the other nonsense he tried to peddle. Just all this just mouth vomit [expletive] that people got sick of.Rodgers has never shied away from sharing opinions beyond football, and those comments have often generated as much attention as his performances on the field. While supporters continue to defend his willingness to speak openly, critics argue that his repeated references to past controversies have overshadowed his football career.As the veteran quarterback enters what could be his final NFL season with the Pittsburgh Steelers, the spotlight remains divided between his pursuit of success on the field and the conversations his off-field comments continue to generate. With expectations high in Pittsburgh, Rodgers now faces the challenge of shifting the focus back to football while the debate surrounding his latest remarks continues.
Article Summary: Aaron rodgers' latest comments on dr. anthony fauci have once again pushed the veteran quarterback into the middle of a heated public debate. Rodgers defended his long-held views during a recent appearance on the pat mcafee show. Fs1 analyst nick wright questioned both the quarterback's credibility and his continued focus on the issue.

Article Title: WNBA commissioner breaks silence on transgender debate after Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White’s 2027 draft declarations, ‘I’m officially declaring…’
Article Text:
WNBA’s Cathy Engelbert breaks silence on transgender debate after Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White’s 2027 draft declarations, ‘I’m officially declaring…’

Cathy Engelbert addresses transgender athlete debate as Enes Kanter Freedom, Royce White declare for WNBA Draft

Sophie Cunningham comments on women’s sports as WNBPA backs inclusion

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has asked teams to prepare for more discussion about transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball, calling the issue one that needs a careful and respectful approach. Her memo comes as the league faces fresh questions after former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White said they plan to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. The debate also grew after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham spoke about protecting women’s sports. Engelbert said team presidents and general managers will discuss the matter at a meeting next week, while the WNBPA has also spoken about inclusion. CAccording to The Associated Press, Engelbert sent the memo to WNBA teams on Friday after the recent attention around transgender participation.She wrote, “I know many of you have received questions in recent weeks regarding transgender athlete participation in women’s basketball, and I expect this topic will continue to receive significant attention.”Engelbert said in the memo obtained by The Associated Press. “I wanted to reach out to share how we are approaching these conversations at the league office and to thank those of you who have responded to questions from the media with thoughtfulness and professionalism.”Engelbert also said the league will discuss the matter with team presidents and general managers next week. She wrote that the WNBA will “always approach this topic thoughtfully, respectfully, and in alignment with the longstanding values of our league. … Preserving the integrity of our game and ensuring fair competition will always remain among the league’s highest priorities.”The memo followed announcements from Freedom and White about the 2027 WNBA Draft. Freedom said he had reviewed the league’s current eligibility rules and was declaring himself a WNBA prospect. White later said he would also enter the draft and said he identifies as transgender.Freedom said, “After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I’m officially declaring myself a WNBA prospect,” before arguing that the rules should apply equally to everyone. The WNBA’s collective bargaining agreement says that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA.”The latest debate follows comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in an ESPN profile published July 21. Cunningham said she had received criticism over her views but rejected the idea that she was attacking transgender people.“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” Cunningham said. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”Cunningham added, “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides. And that’s all I’ve ever said about my political beliefs. But people love to assume.”The WNBPA responded after Freedom’s announcement by stressing its support for different views and inclusion.The union said its members have different experiences, cultures and opinions, while adding that “Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm.” It also said, “We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns.”
Article Summary: Wnba commissioner cathy engelbert asks teams to prepare for more discussion about transgender athlete participation in women's basketball. Former nba players enes kanter freedom and royce white said they plan to enter the 2027 wnba draft. The debate also grew after indiana fever guard sophie cunningham spoke about protecting women’s sports.
